taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: usual 8-20 m, the tallest about 25 m; Reiche (1896) calls it a modest shrub in central Chile and a tall, stout tree in the south.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 202, Drimys winteri: leaves elliptic to oblanceolate, dark green above and whitish below; Reiche (1896, p. 26-27) has them obovate or lanceolate, short-stalked and leathery, the outline between those.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.inflorescence.note: Reiche, Flora de Chile vol. 1 (1896) p. 26-27, Drimys Winteri: flowers alone in the upper leaf axils or in stalked umbels, or both on one plant (Simpson p. 202: an umbel-like cyme).

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.flower_colour.note: Reiche, Flora de Chile vol. 1 (1896) p. 26, Drimys: petals white, 6-24, soon falling (Simpson p. 202: cream-white). The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.fruit_type.note: Reiche, Flora de Chile vol. 1 (1896) p. 26-27, Drimys Winteri: berries blackish.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Reiche, Flora de Chile vol. 1 (1896) p. 26-27, Drimys Winteri: berries blackish. The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: Reiche (1896) has it flowering from May in the north to September at Valdivia.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

generator.params.note: Pacific madrone's crown values, changed by hand: one straight trunk with ascending branches into a narrow crown. Not fitted to measurements. spur_leaf is the leaf card the angiosperm rule gives leaf_size, 1.5 times the flora's mean blade, so short-shoot leaves are drawn the same size.

allometry.note: 15 m at 40 years in the open, within the model estimate's usual 8-20 m. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after Reiche (1896) and Simpson: pale grey bark and red young twigs; glossy leaves, whitish below.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the Magnoliidae specs (2026-10-16): characters from Reiche (1896) and Simpson, sizes from model estimates, drawing values from Pacific madrone's.
